title: MCPs are Boring (or: Why we are losing the Sparkle of LLMs) - Manuel Odendahl
talk_summary: Manuel Odendahl argues that MCP/tool-calling is a bottleneck: too many tools confuse models, arguments and results waste tokens, and static schemas can't express what LLMs can do. His alternative is to give the model a single eval/sandbox tool (JS/SQL/bash) with preloaded libraries, let it write and iterate code, then persist working code as reusable functions/views/APIs.

takeaways.technique: Single eval/sandbox tool instead of many narrow tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose one eval tool with preloaded libraries (SQLite, web handlers) so the model writes code that inspects schema, filters, queries, and aggregates in one call rather than chaining many tool calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: why do we even need MCPS when uh we just have eval?
takeaways.numbers: claims ~500 tokens and deterministic result vs ~5,000 tokens and wrong answer for the multi-tool-call path; example ran in 2-3 seconds in one tool call instead of ~15 tool calls

takeaways.technique: Filter tool results inside code before returning to model
takeaways.what_they_do: Because the model writes code, it can filter/aggregate results in the sandbox and only return the needed rows, instead of dumping full JSON into context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It will actually already filter them. uh so it saves on tokens
takeaways.numbers: example: 2,000 tokens of weather JSON to get one number; 20,000-token CRM dump costing ~50 cents and 5 minutes

takeaways.technique: Persist working code as reusable functions/views/APIs
takeaways.what_they_do: Once the model writes code that solves a query, save it as a named function, SQL view, or REST endpoint so future runs call the cheap deterministic artifact instead of re-deriving it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: once it works you know why not store this query uh why not say like oh now we have like a get customer order amount query

takeaways.technique: Let the model generate the tool it needs from a schema
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of predefining every tool, give the model a DB/API schema and let it write the specific function (e.g. get company contact) on demand.
takeaways.evidence_quote: please create the tool that I want. Right? If I if I give it a database schema
takeaways.numbers: claims even a 3B local model can do this

takeaways.what_they_do: Show the proposed tool call (and its result) to a human/agent for edit before committing, instead of only allow/reject, so a bad query can be fixed without rewinding the whole run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if it's an agent thing I have to rewind the whole agent run instead of being able to edit this one tool

takeaways.technique: Code-execution sandbox as the primary agent interface
takeaways.what_they_do: Run a JS/bash sandbox with loaded libraries and a register-handler web server, so the model can build and serve real artifacts (CRM UI, REST endpoints) from one eval tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I didn't it just give it like JavaScript with loaded libraries is that suddenly I have a JavaScript sandbox
